title: An operator can see the refusal
description: An error channel nobody surfaces closes nothing. Make a non-empty errors array visible where a person or a CI job will actually encounter it: a non-zero exit from `bober run`, and a failed run state in the MCP run manager.

successCriteria.description: `bober run` sets a non-zero process exit code when the result's errors array is non-empty, even when success is true under the Option A formula.
`bober run` prints what was refused -- at minimum the nodeId and errorClass of each entry -- rather than a generic failure line.
The MCP run manager sets RunState.status to "failed" and populates RunState.error when errors is non-empty; neither field needs a schema change.
A run with an empty or absent errors array keeps today's exit code and today's run state exactly -- proven by a test, so the change is additive.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green.

nonGoals: Adding new fields to RunState -- status "failed" and error?: string already exist.
stopConditions: A CI wrapper in this repository depends on `bober run` exiting zero for a refused run -- stop and report it before changing the exit code.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green, and every documentation claim added is backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
generatorNotes: src/cli/commands/run.ts already sets process.exitCode = 1 at :241-242 when !result.success; add a branch rather than restructuring the existing one, and make sure the two do not fight. src/mcp/run-manager.ts already declares status 'failed' (:39) and error?: string (:46) and sets status at :209 and :233 -- follow the existing assignment sites. sc-6-4 is the important one: this must be strictly additive for runs that produced no errors, so write that test first.
evaluatorNotes: Verify the additive claim in sc-6-4 by actually running a clean pipeline and confirming the exit code and run state are unchanged from before the sprint. Verify the exit code genuinely changes for a refused run by executing one end to end, not by unit-testing the branch in isolation. Check the printed output names the refused node -- a message that says 'run failed' without saying what was refused fails sc-6-2.
